summary: Idaho's first NHLR-listed lookout, its current L-4 cabin is the third building on the site and is now a popular Forest Service rental.

access.note: Available via Forest Service recreation rental program (recreation.gov).

visit.trail_note: Reached via Shoshone Ridge Trail #81; rental cabin, not open for casual climbing.

events.note: Original frame cabin built on Guard Peak.
Cupola cabin and crow's-nest built on Downey Peak, 1 mile northwest.
Current L-4 cabin on concrete base built on south summit; NHLR gives 1956, idahofirelookouts/firelookout.com give 1957.
First Idaho lookout listed on the National Historic Lookout Register, October 30, 1990.

evidence.supports: location, 1919 origin, third structure, NHLR first-in-Idaho listing
evidence.quote: The structure standing today on Little Guard Peak is the third in a series of lookout buildings that originated back to 1919. In October 1990, Little Guard Lookout was accepted for listing in the National Historic Lookout Register and the first for Idaho.

evidence.supports: 1919 frame cabin, 1929 cupola cabin, staff list, 1977 emergency status
evidence.quote:
1919 – A frame cabin was built on Guard Peak.
1929 – Cupola cabin & crow's nest was built on Downey Peak.
1977 – Put on emergency staffed status.

evidence.supports: 1957 build year, staffed into 1990s, first on NHLR
evidence.quote: the present 10' concrete slab base with L-4 cab built atop the south summit in 1957, remained actively staffed into the 1990's... The tower was the first Idaho lookout listed on the National Historic Lookout Register.
The fully furnished two-story fire lookout has dimensions of 14 x 14 feet, an external cat walk, and a gabled roof. It sleeps four guests

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1956; firelookout.com and idahofirelookouts.com give 1957. Story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Minor year conflict (1956 vs 1957) for the current cabin's construction, noted in the story and resolved_conflicts. Staff list on idahofirelookouts.com is extensive; only representative names used in the narrative to keep prose readable. Fact-check pass (2026-10-04): the 'nine miles north of Shoshone Camp' and '1 mile northwest' distance details were cited only to single sources in the draft though confirmed on additional sources (idahofirelookouts and recreation.gov both give the 9-mile figure; firelookout.com gives the 1-mile figure); the 1956/1957 build-year sentence was missing its NHLR (cite 1) footnote even though NHLR is the source of the 1956 date and dimensions. All three citation gaps fixed in the story.
